stories.summary: infinitSpace, a European flexible workspace provider, is entering the U.S. market with a 32,000-square-foot coworking location at the Desmond's Building in Downtown Los Angeles, opening November 2, 2026. The space will accommodate approximately 400 memberships across private offices, shared workspaces, meeting rooms, and lounges, with an option to expand to 40,500 SF. The company plans to open 30 U.S. locations over the next 24 months using an asset-light management model where property owners retain ownership while infinitSpace operates the workspace.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development. Coworking expansion is office-focused and unlikely to create direct demand signals for apartments, though the firm's capital influx and U.S. growth may modestly increase office worker density in DTLA, which could marginally support renter demand in nearby residential submarkets. Effect is secondary and minimal.

stories.title: Private Equity Firm Expands at SL Green’s One Vanderbilt
stories.excerpt: SL Green Realty Corp. announced that private equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners has signed a lease expansion covering 7,134 square feet on a portion of the 54th floor at One Vanderbilt Ave. The expansion increases the tenant’s total commitment within the building to 34,737 square feet. “We’re proud to expand our valued relationship with Sentinel and support their growth by more than 25 percent at One Vanderbilt Avenue,” said Steven Durels, EVP and director of leasing and real property at SL Green. “This transaction is another example of the strong leasing momentum we’re seeing at the building and across our portfolio.” SL Green recently announced it has signed 130 Manhattan office leases totaling 1,794,126 square feet year to date. The REIT’s current office leasing pipeline has also increased to more than 1.0 million square feet. Sentinel Capital Partners was represented by Brian Waterman and David Waterman of Newmark. SL Green was represented in-house. The post Private Equity Firm Expands at SL Green’s One Vanderbilt appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sentinel Capital Partners expands 34% (7,134 SF) at SL Green's One Vanderbilt, Manhattan
SL Green signed 130 office leases YTD totaling 1.79M SF; pipeline exceeds 1.0M SF
Strong leasing momentum at trophy office asset signals financial services job retention/growth in Midtown
stories.summary: Private equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners has signed a lease expansion of 7,134 square feet at One Vanderbilt Avenue in Manhattan, increasing its total commitment to 34,737 SF (a 25%+ expansion). SL Green reported 130 Manhattan office leases year-to-date totaling 1.79 million square feet, with a leasing pipeline exceeding 1.0 million SF. The expansion demonstrates sustained demand from institutional tenants at flagship Manhattan office.
stories.impact: Midtown Manhattan office leasing momentum signals continued high-paying job stability in finance and professional services, supporting rental demand for Class A apartments in Midtown East, Murray Hill, and Kips Bay submarkets. Multifamily operators should monitor if this leasing strength persists—sustained corporate growth and employment stability in Midtown translates to stronger renter demographics and rent growth potential for new or existing apartment inventory in the core Manhattan market.

stories.title: Westwood Financial Acquires Grocery-Anchored Huntington Beach Center
stories.excerpt: Westwood Financial has acquired Peninsula Marketplace, a 95,416-square-foot, Ralphs-anchored shopping center in Huntington Beach, for an undisclosed amount The property is 99% leased. The acquisition comes as Southern California’s retail market continues to strengthen, according to Westwood. In the second quarter of 2026, Orange County led Greater Los Angeles in positive net absorption. Westwood is seeing similar momentum across its own portfolio, with its owned Southern California portfolio more than 99% leased at the end of the first half of 2026. “Peninsula Marketplace is a substantial addition to our portfolio,” said Lauren Ball, COO at Westwood Financial. “Grocery-anchored retail has been a key driver of Westwood’s success for nearly 60 years, and over that time, we’ve developed a deep understanding of what differentiates one opportunity from the next. With a strong anchor like Ralphs, which has been operating at this location for more than two decades, Peninsula Marketplace is fully integrated into the Huntington Beach community. As a legacy owner and operator in Southern California, we’re excited about the opportunities ahead as the market continues to strengthen.” The post Westwood Financial Acquires Grocery-Anchored Huntington Beach Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Westwood Financial acquires Peninsula Marketplace: 95,416 SF, Ralphs-anchored, Huntington Beach, 99% leased
Orange County led Greater Los Angeles in Q2 2026 positive net absorption; Westwood portfolio 99%+ leased

stories.summary: Westwood Financial acquired Peninsula Marketplace, a 95,416-square-foot Ralphs-anchored shopping center in Huntington Beach, at 99% occupancy. Orange County led Greater Los Angeles in positive net absorption in Q2 2026, and Westwood's own Southern California portfolio is running 99%+ leased. The firm views grocery-anchored retail as a key growth driver after nearly 60 years in the format.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Strong retail absorption and grocery anchor stability in Orange County may support demand for convenience-oriented apartments near shopping centers (especially in Huntington Beach and surrounding OC markets), but this is a secondary signal—retail health reflects consumer confidence and foot traffic, not direct apartment demand drivers. Multifamily operators should note OC's positive absorption as a proxy for local economic health and potential renter stability.

stories.title: Family Dollar Closes $75M Sale-Leaseback for 47 Retail Locations
stories.excerpt: JLL and GA Group Real Estate announced today that it closed a $74.7 million sale-leaseback for a 47-property Family Dollar retail portfolio totaling 387,945 square feet across 19 states. JLL’s Net Lease Team and GA Group Real Estate exclusively represented the seller, FD Retail Properties LLC. The assets were acquired by an institutional real estate investor. The geographically diverse portfolio provides institutional investors with built-in risk mitigation through its coast-to-coast, multi-state footprint and reliable, long-term tenancy. The deal structure provides the financial flexibility to accelerate growth initiatives while ensuring the retailer maintains its footprint and operational continuity across all locations. This marks JLL and GA Group’s second major Family Dollar portfolio closing in 2026, following a $75 million transaction for a 46-property portfolio that closed earlier this year. stories.summary: JLL and GA Group completed a $74.7 million sale-leaseback of a 47-property Family Dollar portfolio totaling 387,945 square feet across 19 states. This is the second major Family Dollar portfolio JLL and GA Group closed in 2026, following a $75 million transaction for 46 properties. The sale-leaseback structure provides financial flexibility while allowing the retailer to maintain operational continuity.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. Family Dollar's capital raise via sale-leaseback is a financing tool for retail operations, not a signal of market disruption or dislocation that would affect apartment supply or demand. However, institutional investors' appetite for lower-cost retail anchors across 19 states suggests broad confidence in discount retail's resilience, which may support demand for Class C and workforce apartments near these discount retailers in secondary and tertiary markets.

stories.title: BXP Sells D.C. Office to Jemal Equities for $92M
stories.excerpt: BXP has unloaded a 254,000-square-foot office building in Washington, D.C.’s Dupont Circle for $92.3 million as the firm sheds older properties in the nation’s capital. Affiliates of Jemal Equities acquired the building at 1330 Connecticut Avenue NW, according to deed records cited by the Business Journals. Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust provided $72.5 million in financing for the deal. Douglas Development Managing Principal Matthew Jemal runs Jemal Equities. The acquisition is the company’s fourth D.C. office purchase in about 14 months in deals totaling almost $227 million. In May, the firm acquired a 235,000-square-foot office building at 99 M Street SE for $93.2 million from an affiliate of Polinger. A month earlier, it purchased the 155,000-square-foot Lion Building at 1233 20th Street NW from affiliates of MRP Realty and BGO for $12.4 million. Jemal Equities also acquired the 123,000-square-foot property at 1750 H Street NW for $28.8 million last year. For BXP, the disposition is part of a broader strategy to sell older D.C. office assets while directing capital toward new trophy office developments. The Boston-based real estate investment trust is developing projects at 725 12th Street NW and 2100 M Street NW, both pre-leased to law firms. The properties represent the only new private office construction in D.C.’s pipeline. The company also transferred its leasehold interest in the 210,000-square-foot Sumner Square office complex to an affiliate of Vieron Capital for $63 million in August. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BXP sells 254,000 SF office building, 1330 Connecticut Ave NW, Washington D.C. for $92.3M to Jemal Equities

stories.summary: Boston Properties sold a 254,000-square-foot office building at 1330 Connecticut Avenue NW in Washington, D.C.'s Dupont Circle to Jemal Equities for $92.3 million. Burke & Herbert Bank & Trust provided $72.5 million in financing. This is Jemal Equities' fourth D.C. office acquisition in approximately 14 months, totaling nearly $227 million, signaling aggressive pursuit of repositioning opportunities in the nation's capital.
stories.impact: BXP's exit from aging D.C. office is part of sector-wide office shedding; Jemal's rapid accumulation of D.C. office at scale suggests confidence in future office repositioning and conversion potential (including possible adaptive reuse to residential or mixed-use). Multifamily operators should monitor Jemal's next moves—if a portfolio of 600K+ SF of core D.C. office is repositioned toward residential or mixed-use, it could signal demand for conversions or new supply in Central D.C. submarkets (Dupont Circle, Downtown, NoMa) and signal distress-level pricing opportunities for acquiring aging office for development.

stories.title: Arrow Linen Site in Park Slope Sells for Residential Development
stories.excerpt: JLL Capital Markets arranged the $55-million sale of 441–467 Prospect Ave., a residential development site in Brooklyn’s Park Slope neighborhood. The team of Mike Mazzara, Ethan Stanton and Brendan Maddigan represented Arrow Linen Supply Company in the sale and negotiated directly with the buyer, Goose Property Management. The site occupies two lots on the north side of Prospect Avenue between Prospect Park West and Eighth Avenue, near Prospect Park and the 15th Street–Prospect Park subway station. The site offers 271,000 square feet of potential zoning floor area for residential development. A spokesperson for Arrow Linen said, “Arrow Linen has been proud to call Brooklyn its home since 1947. Recently, after the unexpected passing of our CEO and majority shareholder, the remaining shareholders elected to longer be part of the site’s development. We are confident that the new team will bring badly needed homes, including affordable homes, to Brooklyn.” The post Arrow Linen Site in Park Slope Sells for Residential Development appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: JLL Capital Markets brokered the $55 million sale of a 441–467 Prospect Avenue development site in Brooklyn's Park Slope neighborhood. The two-lot site offers 271,000 square feet of zoning floor area for residential development. Goose Property Management acquired the property from Arrow Linen Supply Company, a family business that had operated in Brooklyn since 1947. The site is located near Prospect Park and the 15th Street–Prospect Park subway station.
stories.impact: Strong signal for Park Slope residential development pipeline. The $55M price and seller's explicit mention of 'badly needed homes, including affordable homes' suggest market demand for residential density near Prospect Park and strong transit access. Goose Property Management's acquisition signals builder or investor confidence in Park Slope rents and development feasibility. Monitor for entitlement timelines—this is a key infill site that could add significant units to a high-demand, supply-constrained Brooklyn submarket. Strong public perception of housing shortage also reducing political barriers to development.

stories.title: Educational Nonprofit Signs Lease to Build Campus on Brooklyn’s Floyd Bennett Field
stories.excerpt: The National Park Service has leased a 7-acre space in Brooklyn’s Marine Park neighborhood to a workforce development nonprofit. Runway Green signed a 60-year agreement with the federal government to build a $60 million agricultural and environmental education facility at Floyd Bennett Field, according to the organization. The former airfield near Jamaica Bay is within Gateway National Recreation Area, which the Park Service oversees. The first phase of the project will break ground next year when 3 acres will be dedicated to urban farming in partnership with the Campaign Against Hunger. “This lease turns a bold vision into a public commitment to New York City’s young people,” Geoff Roehm, founder and executive director of Runway Green, said in a statement. “At Floyd Bennett Field, we will build an educational ecosystem where schools, employers, nonprofits, colleges and public agencies work together to create learning experiences no single institution could provide on its own.” A rendering of Runway Green’s proposed education campus at Floyd Bennett Field, Brooklyn. RENDERING: Courtesy ARO, SCAPE, Colloqate Runway Green has already raised $9.3 million toward its $60 million budget from a mix of government sources, such as $1 million from Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso, $3.3 million from the New York City Council and funding from the federal government. Once completed, Runway Green’s facility will serve up to 50,000 New York City public school students per year, according to the organization. “Runway Green will equip New York City students with the skills and experiences they need to succeed while making one of Brooklyn’s great public assets more accessible, engaging and meaningful to the communities it serves,” U.S. Sen. Charles Schumer said in a statement. The organization plans to build a $60 million agricultural and environmental education facility, with the first phase breaking ground in 2027. The project will include 3 acres of urban farming in partnership with the Campaign Against Hunger.
stories.impact: Limited direct impact on multifamily; however, long-term federal land activation near Jamaica Bay and Gateway National Recreation Area could signal future neighborhood amenity enhancement and stabilization in Marine Park/Floyd Bennett Field area. If successful, the workforce development and education programming could attract younger, lower-income renter populations and increase demand for Class C/workforce housing in the broader Canarsie/Marine Park submarkets. Minimal near-term impact; worth monitoring for secondary effects on neighborhood trajectory over 10+ years.

stories.title: European Coworking Firm Enters U.S. With 32K-SF Lease in Downtown L.A.
stories.excerpt: European flexible workspace operator InfinitSpace is entering the U.S. market with a 32,000-square-foot location in Downtown Los Angeles, its first step in a plan to open 30 locations nationwide in the next two years. The company announced Tuesday that it has entered into a long-term management partnership at the historic Desmond’s Building at 612 South Broadway. The new coworking spot, operating under infinitSpace’s Beyond brand, is scheduled to open Nov. 2. The workspace will occupy the second through fifth floors of the building, accommodating approximately 400 memberships with private offices, shared workspaces, meeting rooms and lounges. It will also feature a rooftop event space. An option for the sixth floor could add another 8,500 square feet, for about 40,500 square feet total. Unlike traditional coworking operators that lease space directly from landlords, InfinitSpace uses an asset-light management model in which property owners retain ownership and long-term control of their buildings. The company handles workspace operations, sales, marketing and technology, including an artificial intelligence platform designed to automate administrative tasks. The Los Angeles opening will mark InfinitSpace’s 15th location worldwide. The company serves more than 8,000 members on three continents, and expects to reach approximately 10,000 members by year’s end. Its initial U.S. expansion will focus on Los Angeles, San Francisco, Austin, Seattle and New York. “Property owners are looking for ways to make their buildings more productive and responsive to how companies use space, while businesses want flexibility without compromising the quality of their workplace,” InfinitSpace CEO and co-founder Wybo Wijnbergen said in a statement. “Our partnership model and technology were built to address both needs.” The Desmond’s Building opened in 1924 in Downtown L.A.’s Broadway Theatre District as the flagship store of clothing retailer Desmond’s. Secondary effect only—primary driver of apartment demand remains office employment density and wage growth, not coworking supply.

stories.title: Investor Daryl Hagler Takes Over Ridgewood’s Embattled Resi Tower Development
stories.excerpt: Real estate investor and controversial health care mogul Daryl Hagler has signed on the dotted line to take over one of the most embattled developments in Ridgewood, Queens. The under-construction mixed-use tower at 3-50 St. Nicholas Avenue changed hands Tuesday for $75.8 million in cash, according to city records, with entities tied to troubled developer Arch Companies and Meir Babaev’s AB Capstone conveying the development to Hagler’s CDK 3-50 St. Nicholas. Toronto-based investor Kevin Wiener, whose family office 35 Oak Holdings previously partnered with developers Arch and AB Capstone, signed for the seller entities. Spokespeople for Arch, Wiener and Capstone could not be immediately reached for comment. The 252,850-square-foot structure, bounded by Ridgewood’s Palmetto Street, Myrtle Avenue and Nicholas Avenue, is slated to host 133 residential units, as well as a large retail component. A Burlington location quietly opened its doors there this month, Grimes Square reported, but the apartments remain unoccupied. The site secured a certificate of occupancy in August, according to Department of Buildings records. The transaction on Tuesday left in place mortgages from Madison Realty Capital with outstanding amounts totaling $75 million, with Hagler’s CDK LLC assuming the debt obligations. Hagler also secured the 99-year ground lease for an accompanying parcel for $10.2 million, according to the filing. A spokesperson for Madison declined to comment. Jeffrey Simpson and Jared Chassen’s Arch Companies purchased a stake in the project from Babaev’s Capstone in 2021, according to Crain’s New York Business. Brothers Kevin and Michael Wiener also joined the project as investors. The project, most recently dubbed the Ridgewood, was mired in community pushback from its earliest days. bullets: CDK Capital's Daryl Hagler acquires 3-50 St. Nicholas Ave., Ridgewood, Queens for $75.8M in cash

stories.summary: Real estate investor Daryl Hagler's CDK Capital has acquired the under-construction mixed-use tower at 3-50 St. Nicholas Avenue in Ridgewood, Queens for $75.8 million in cash. The 252,850-square-foot development is slated to include 133 residential units and a large retail component. The acquisition transfers the troubled project from developers Arch Companies and Meir Babaev's AB Capstone to new ownership. A Burlington location recently opened retail space, but apartments remain unoccupied.
stories.impact: Significant signal of distressed multifamily development restructuring in Queens. Hagler's takeover of 133-unit Ridgewood tower at what may be a discount suggests earlier developer/financier stress, likely driven by construction cost overruns, financing challenges, or pre-leasing shortfalls. The ability to absorb the project at $75.8M signals investor confidence in Ridgewood rents and neighborhood trajectory, but the 133 units coming to market may face lease-up challenges depending on pricing. Monitor absorption closely—delays or price pressure in Ridgewood would signal broader construction cost/financing pressures affecting Queens multifamily starts and underwriting.

stories.title: EliseAI, Manhattan-Based Proptech Unicorn, Raises $350M
stories.excerpt: EliseAI, an artificial intelligence company automating housing and health care systems, announced Tuesday that it has raised $350 million, bringing the proptech unicorn’s valuation to $4 billion. Andreessen Horowitz (also known as a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, with participation from the Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Sapphire Ventures and Navitas Capital. EliseAI will use the capital to accelerate the development and delivery of new products, automating more of its customers’ operations, and to grow its engineering, deployment and sales teams across its North American offices. Additionally, it plans to establish San Francisco as a second engineering hub alongside its Manhattan headquarters. “Our customers ask us to support more of their operations every year, and we raised now so we can keep pace with that demand,” Minna Song, co-founder and CEO of EliseAI, told Commercial Observer. “We’re investing in a second engineering hub in San Francisco alongside New York, and we’re hiring across engineering, deployment, and sales in New York, Boston, Chicago, Austin and Toronto. We’re investing in building a product that handles the daily work of running a building: leasing, renewals, maintenance, collections and the questions residents send at all hours.” EliseAI bills itself as the only AI product in the space to work with all property types, from conventional multifamily to scattered-site and single-family properties to student and affordable properties, as well as properties managed locally and through centralization. In June 2026, EliseAI announced that it had surpassed $200 million in annual recurring revenue, doubling revenue year-over-year for five consecutive years. The platform now powers one in six U.S. apartments, and more than 30 million Americans have interacted with EliseAI since its founding, according to the company. stories.summary: EliseAI, a Manhattan-based proptech unicorn, announced a $350 million Series C funding round at a $4 billion valuation. Andreessen Horowitz and Bessemer Venture Partners led the round, with participation from Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Sapphire Ventures, and Navitas Capital. The company plans to establish San Francisco as a second engineering hub and expand hiring across North American offices in New York, Boston, Chicago, and Austin.
stories.impact: Positive signal for multifamily technology adoption and operational efficiency gains across the industry. EliseAI's $4B valuation and $350M raise reflect strong investor belief in AI-driven automation of housing operations (rent collection, maintenance, tenant communications, compliance). Expansion to San Francisco and Austin reflects demand from multifamily operators in high-growth markets. For Trammell Crow and peer developers: rising adoption of EliseAI and similar platforms suggests improving operational margins for existing portfolio companies, but also increased competitive pressure to adopt automation. Monitor if major operators standardize on EliseAI—could indicate shift in how multifamily deals are underwritten and valued going forward.
